title: Process Hardening V1 — reproducible review, durable receipts, and enforced state transitions
description: Six bounded packets extracted from the 2026-07-25 process-hardening proposals. This initiative is separate from KittyBuilder Brain V1 so it can be launched independently or sequenced after the visible cockpit work. Each packet must preserve history, reuse existing Builder and context machinery, and avoid unrelated product work.

packets.title: Immutable review freeze
packets.objective: Add a review-freeze command or script that resolves a branch, tag, or commit to a full immutable SHA and writes a machine-readable freeze record containing target SHA, base SHA, branch/ref, changed files, timestamp, and dirty-tree status. Refuse dirty trees by default; an explicit allow-dirty override must mark the freeze unreproducible.
acceptance_criteria: Branches and tags resolve to full immutable SHAs
Dirty trees fail by default and explicit override is visibly unreproducible
Changed files are computed against the recorded base
Invalid refs and invalid bases fail loudly
Tests cover clean, dirty, detached HEAD, explicit base, and invalid-ref cases
Minimal operator documentation exists

packets.title: Review by SHA and owned scope
packets.objective: Create a review contract containing frozen review SHA, base SHA, owned paths, excluded paths, freeze-record reference, and reviewer identity. Reject branch-only review targets, stale/missing freeze records, and changed files outside owned scope. Findings must identify file/location or symbol and reviewed SHA. Reuse existing Builder scope logic rather than creating competing path semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Valid frozen review inside owned paths passes
Branch-only review target fails
Out-of-scope changed path fails loudly
Deleted and renamed files are handled
Findings retain the reviewed SHA
Tests cover files, directories, exclusions, overlap, renames, deletion, and violations

packets.title: Immutable session receipts
packets.objective: Add one immutable receipt per session plus an atomically updated CURRENT.json pointer. Build on gateway/context_receipt.py rather than introducing a competing continuity system. Receipts include branch, HEAD, base, working-tree state, timestamp, task, completed work, remaining work, decisions, uncertainty, and artifacts. Validate receipts and recover when CURRENT.json is missing, corrupt, or points to a missing receipt. Do not delete legacy STATE.md or HANDOFF.md in this packet.
acceptance_criteria: Existing receipts are never modified
CURRENT.json updates atomically under a lock
Concurrent writers cannot produce partial or crossed pointers
Recovery locates the newest valid receipt
Invalid receipts fail schema validation clearly
Tests cover concurrency, corruption, missing target, dirty tree, and detached HEAD

packets.title: Live versus snapshot authority API
packets.objective: Create explicit live() and snapshot(at=...) state read paths. live() reflects current repository/runtime state; snapshot() reconstructs from an immutable receipt or frozen SHA and never silently falls back to live data. Every result includes provenance: mode, commit SHA, timestamp, receipt/freeze identifier when applicable, dirty status, and sources used. Remove or wrap ambiguous generic loaders.
acceptance_criteria: live() reflects current state
snapshot() remains stable after working-tree changes
Missing snapshot data fails loudly without live fallback
Every result includes provenance
Callers can distinguish stale snapshot from current state
Tests prove live/snapshot divergence and stable reconstruction

packets.title: Single state writer and architectural enforcement
packets.objective: Designate one canonical writer for session receipts, current-pointer updates, approved mutable continuity state, locking, atomic writes, and schema validation. Add an architectural test that rejects unauthorized direct writes to protected state paths or low-level persistence helpers. Maintain a small explicit allowlist with module, operation, reason, owner, and removal condition.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical writers pass architectural checks
Unauthorized direct-write fixture fails and identifies file and operation
Read-only access is not falsely classified as a write
Protected paths are centrally declared
Allowlist exceptions require documented reason, owner, and removal condition
Existing legitimate writers are migrated or explicitly justified

packets.title: Builder transition hardening
packets.objective: Create one declarative Builder transition table and route all task state changes through one guarded transition function. Metadata includes allowed/denied, required preconditions, terminal behavior, retry semantics, required actor/requester, and audit event. Undeclared transitions, invalid backwards transitions, terminal reopening, and silent no-ops fail loudly. Recovery and reconciliation must use the same rules. Convert silent-transition detection into a required assertion.
acceptance_criteria: Every existing Builder task transition is declared
Valid transitions preserve expected behavior
Undeclared and invalid transitions fail loudly
Terminal states cannot reopen accidentally
Idempotent requests have explicit tested behavior
Every successful transition records actor, reason, previous state, next state, and event
Direct mutation outside the transition function is detected
Queue doctor/silent-transition assertion passes
validation_commands: python3.12 -m pytest tests/test_builder_transitions.py tests/test_builder_queue.py tests/test_builder_loop.py tests/test_builder_run.py -q --tb=short
